candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — therapeutic drug safety
candidate.educational_objective: Explain why narrow therapeutic index drugs require precise dosing and, when indicated, close monitoring.

options.A: Small differences in dose or blood concentration can lead to therapeutic failure or serious adverse effects, so careful dosing and monitoring may be important.
options.B: The drug is safe at any dose because toxic concentrations cannot be reached.
options.C: Blood concentration is never clinically relevant for this type of drug.
options.D: The drug has no meaningful relationship between dose and adverse effects.

candidate.rationale: FDA describes narrow therapeutic index drugs as products for which small differences in dose or blood concentration may lead to serious therapeutic failures or serious adverse drug reactions.
candidate.source_claim_supported: NTI drugs have a small margin between effective and harmful exposure such that small dose/concentration differences can have important consequences.
candidate.source_document_title: Narrow Therapeutic Index Drugs / Product-Specific Bioequivalence Guidance
candidate.source_locator: NTI concept: small dose or blood-concentration differences may cause serious therapeutic failures or adverse drug reactions
candidate.stem: Which statement best describes a narrow therapeutic index drug?
